prompt_en:
Create a vertical photorealistic fine-art fashion portrait on a luminous blue shoreline at low tide. One unmistakably adult woman in her mid-twenties steps through clear ankle-deep water while steadying the brim of her natural woven straw hat. She wears an airy ankle-length white linen sundress and carries a small warm smile. A shoulder-height 70 mm portrait view is caught as her forward step touches the water; serene beauty leads the first glance.

This normal coherent world obeys one precisely broken law: one spatial coordinate rule fails. One invisible spatial coordinate law fractures the scene into three depth-aware parallel displacement bands. The face is the largest and strongest convergence point. A bold central band crosses her eyes, nose, and smile by six centimeters, while each displaced facial fragment retains complete eye, nose, mouth, skin, and lighting coherence. Each band shifts every intersected surface by the same exact lateral distance. The same displacement repeats across surfaces. The same offset continues through her hat brim, hair, wet-sand reflection, dress folds, waterline, and distant horizon. Along the fault edges, fine square spatial particles expose the displaced blue sea behind them, obeying the same spacing and direction. Depth-correct parallax and occlusion place the bands inside photographed space; every affected material follows the same six-centimeter rightward offset. The sea breaks through her face by one exact measure.

The unaffected scene remains coherent: intact anatomy, fabric, perspective, sunlight, sand, and water preserve an ordinary physical baseline. Natural lens and sensor response remain optically clean. Only physical consequences identify the fault. The face becomes the second-look rupture; the repeated offset reveals one world law. Three matched displacement bands make one deliberate coordinate-system failure unmistakable from the photograph alone, and three matched contradictions make one authored world rule unmistakable. The result is a quiet second-look contradiction.
